reason: The cited evidence discusses general high-temperature tribo-oxidation and glaze layer formation (E1) and Mn segregation/oxidation in a different alloy (E2), but neither provides specific support for copper segregation, Cu-rich oxide formation, or its role as a lubricious, deformation-limiting tribolayer in FeNiCrCoCu.
premises: Copper selectively segregates to the surface of FeNiCrCoCu at 600°C under low oxygen partial pressure
The segregated copper oxidizes to form a Cu-rich oxide layer
The Cu-rich oxide layer is adherent and acts as a tribolayer during sliding
This tribolayer reduces friction and limits subsurface dislocation motion/deformation
The tribolayer thereby enhances wear resistance at high temperature
